title: Best Sleepy Pokemon Cards
description: A curated shortlist of standout sleeping Pokemon cards, from iconic grails to cozy binder-friendly picks. These are the cards I would start with for a collection that feels beautiful, varied, and fun to collect.
seoTitle: The Best Sleeping Pokemon Cards: Our Favorite Sleepy Art
metaDescription: A personal shortlist of sleeping Pokemon cards, from the Dragonite V grail and cozy Pikachu scenes to beloved favorites like Bulbasaur, Snorlax, and Munna.

cards.reason: Somewhere between sky and nap, Dragonite has become the grail that makes collectors stop scrolling.
Munna drifts beneath a crescent moon while two tiny Pidove sleep along the ledge below, easy to miss in Teeziro’s dreamy pink scene.
Adventure can wait: Akari and Pikachu are both out beneath the tree, still curled close together.
After that feast, nobody is getting Tyranitar back up. The empty dishes make the case.
Curled among the folded clothes in an open drawer, Dedenne has found a hiding place that looks softer than any proper bed.
Asako Ito turns Snorlax into a knitted daydream; even the tiny felt flowers look ready for bed.
The attack is called Nap. The knitted Pikachu is asleep. Exhibit A rests.
Yoriyuki Ikegami gives Bulbasaur a quiet patch of morning sunshine, with broad leaves overhead and not a care in sight.
Even a guardian of emotion needs a quiet minute above Lake Verity. This one feels suspended in a dream.
Raichu is fast asleep on a bed, paws tucked in and eyes closed while sunlight spills across the room. Toshinao Aoki gives this bedroom nap a wonderfully peaceful feel.
A little dream logic, a lot of Komiya character. Drowzee makes the sleepy shortlist feel delightfully odd.
Oshawott has nodded off in a striped hammock above the ocean, with bright beach flowers framing the gentle sway. OKACHEKE makes this seaside nap look like an ideal afternoon.
The old-school blueprint: enormous Snorlax, Eevee along for the ride, and comic-book Zs. Still perfect.
Look between the garden stones: the little trickster has dropped the illusion and gone still.
One bright pink Pawmi stays awake among its sleeping companions, who are tucked into and piled across a hollow log. REND turns their group nap into a sunlit woodland hideaway.
Larvesta is sprawled on a cushioned pet bed, completely at ease as a beam of window light crosses the room. Whisker’s quiet indoor scene makes the little fire moth look especially cozy.

title: Sleepy Full Art Cards
description: On a full art card the nap takes up the whole card, with no frame around the art. Here are fifteen of our favorites: a Sword & Shield alt art, Trainer Gallery and Galarian Gallery cards, Special Illustration Rares, Illustration Rares, and one Chinese card worth tracking down.
seoTitle: Sleeping Pokemon Full Art & Illustration Rare Cards
metaDescription: 15 sleeping Pokemon full art cards: the Skuntank V alt art, Jacq and Bianca's Devotion SIRs, and Illustration Rares like Bulbasaur, Lechonk and Rowlet.

cards.reason: Look past the two Skuntank on guard outside, down into the burrow under the tree roots. Two tiny Stunky are curled up asleep next to the family’s fruit stash, the best nap on the card hiding where you’d look last.
A Special Illustration Rare for anyone who has fallen asleep studying. Jacq is face down at his desk with his glasses still on, a mug and a landslide of books and papers around him.

Lechonk’s flavor text says it spends all day searching for food. Mission accomplished: the bowl is tipped over, crumbs are everywhere, and Lechonk has flopped down on the checkered tiles with its eyes shut.

A pod of Spheal dozing on the ice floes under a bright sun, except the one in the middle, eyes wide open and diving into the water. Its attack, Powder Snow, puts the opponent to sleep, so the others are covered.
Trainer Gallery cards pair a Pokémon with its trainer, and these two make a good team: Ace Trainer Dara reads her map in the curl of Druddigon's body while Druddigon dozes with its head down.
Count the Pidove: nearly every one has flopped over asleep on the cobblestones. The one in the middle is still staring straight at you.

People can tell the season by Sawsbuck’s antlers, says its flavor text. These are thick with summer leaves, and Sawsbuck is stretched out asleep in the long grass beneath them, practically part of the meadow.
Misty has dozed off against Lapras's shell, smiling, while Lapras gazes out to sea. A beach day for two, and only one of them is still awake.
Darumaka is said to fall asleep once the fire inside it dies down. This Illustration Rare catches that exact moment: sitting bolt upright on its cushion, eyes closed, not moving an inch.

Rowlet supposedly likes tight, dark places, like the inside of its Trainer’s bag. Not today: it has dozed off out in the open, a round little ball among bright green leaves, eyes squeezed into happy arcs.

Bianca has crashed on the couch, curled into the cushions with her bag still on, and Musharna dozes right above her. All soft light and warm colors, it's one of the coziest Special Illustration Rares around.

Solrock's own flavor text says it gives off light like the sun when it spins. In this Galarian Gallery card the sun has set, the sky is turning purple, and Solrock has stopped spinning to doze in the flowers while Volbeat and Illumise take over the lighting.
What’s one more plant on a sunny windowsill? Bulbasaur has curled up among the pots for a nap, ignoring the two Pidgey dropping in through the window.
Professor Kukui is down on the floor with a cloth, cleaning up. Rockruff is belly up on the rug, eyes shut and tongue out, contributing nothing.

One for collectors who look beyond English sets: a Simplified Chinese Gem Pack card. Two Cubone sit together on a stone bridge at dusk under a street lamp, one leaning on the other with its eye closed, the gentlest scene on this list.

title: The Sleepiest of Pikachus
description: Every sleepy Pikachu currently in the collection, plus one extremely important cameo where Pikachu sneaks a nap into someone else’s card. Pikachu is always doing excellent work.
seoTitle: Sleeping Pikachu Cards: The Sleepiest of Pikachus
metaDescription: Every sleeping Pikachu card in the collection: Pikachu from the Lost Origin Trainer Gallery, 30th Celebration and the 2024 Illustration Contest promo, plus a Munna cameo.

cards.reason: Pikachu and Akari are both completely out under a tree. The centerpiece pick, and an extremely strong argument for taking the afternoon off.
A tiny knitted Pikachu enjoying a tiny grassy nap. The attack is literally called Nap, so the research has been done for us.
Pikachu fell asleep on a tropical beach and called it Tropical Vibes. Honestly, no notes.
Not asleep yet, but that eyes-shut, full-body yawn says the nap is minutes away. A fan painting that won the 2024 Illustration Contest, with an attack called Unwind.
Munna is the star, but Pikachu is the one fast asleep, tucked under a flowery quilt with Eevee. Munna eats bad dreams, so this nap is in very good hands.

title: Sleepy Cat Pokemon Cards
description: Every sleepy cat Pokemon card currently in the collection, researched with junior Pokemon researcher Linkcat: tiny kittens, dramatic big cats, psychic cats, electric cats, and a few cat-adjacent creatures making a very convincing case. We do not discriminate here.
metaDescription: Browse 24 sleepy cat Pokemon cards featuring Meowth, Litten, Sprigatito, Skitty, Glameow, Espurr, Meowstic, Incineroar, Luxio, Zeraora, Mew, Espeon, Umbreon, and Eevee.

cards.reason: Skitty is a kitten curled up in a tiny bed. No debate, no notes, full marks for understanding the assignment.
A literal Fire Cat enjoying a warm, very committed nap. Litten may be the purest expression of this guide.
Books are flying, Chespin is mid-leap across the room, and Litten has curled up on the armchair with its face buried, ignoring all of it.
The Grass Cat has found a sunny patch and made the only reasonable decision: absolutely nothing for a while.
This cat knows how to cat-nap, and frankly, the collection is willing to respect the craft.
Another Meowth, another excellent cat-nap. Repetition only proves that Meowth has done the research.
The original Scratch Cat brings a wonderfully affordable doze to the page. Sleepy cats are for every binder budget.
Team Rocket's Meowth adds a little theatrical trouble to the cat pile, then promptly needs a lie-down.
Technically a card about Bebe. But the most cat thing on it is Glameow, asleep beside her laptop, so in it goes.
Emma’s Espurr, Mimi, asleep at the office. Unmistakably feline, deeply psychic, and very much off duty.
This Espurr’s own attack is called Caturday, and it ends with Espurr falling Asleep. Stretched out mid-yawn under a tree, it has clearly been practicing.
Meowstic has flattened itself across a sunny rug by the window, eyes shut. Anyone who has lived with a cat knows this exact pose.
Litten's fully evolved big-cat form proves that even a dramatic wrestling heel needs a proper recovery nap.
Luxio has curled up on a pink pillow hugging a teddy bear, one eye already shut and the other not far behind.
This is the Zeraora that belongs here: flat on its back in a meadow of white flowers, eyes shut, arms flung wide. Its card says it moves at the speed of lightning. Not today.
Mew is our mythical, cat-shaped technicality. The ears, paws, tail, and excellent sleeping form make a persuasive case.
Our cat-shaped technicality again, this time drifting through a blossoming forest with its eyes half closed. Not quite asleep, but very much on the way.
Espeon is the clearly feline Eeveelution, here in spectacularly oversized sleepy-cat form.
Umbreon is lying in bed looking one blink away from sleep. Cat, cat-adjacent, or moon creature: admitted.
A second sleepy Umbreon strengthens the case. We remain open-minded when the evidence is this cozy.
Curled into a tight ball with its rings glowing, which is about the most cat way to sleep there is. Karen’s Umbreon makes the case all by itself.
Stretched out on a rooftop above the city, mid-yawn. If that isn’t cat behavior, nothing in this guide is.
Eevee is famously a little cat, dog, and fox at once. That is more than enough cat for this collection.
A whole litter of Eevee has taken over the living room, and several have already given up: one hugging a plush on the couch, another curled up in a basket in the corner.

title: Sleepy Pokemon Cameos
description: Sometimes the featured Pokemon is wide awake, but another sleeper quietly steals the scene. These cameos reward a closer look, and this growing shelf is here to help you spot them.
metaDescription: Find sleeping Pokemon cameos in card art, from Pidove and Teddiursa to Sewaddle, Pachirisu, Psyduck, Mareep, Glameow, Cosmog, and even a sleeping Drayton.

cards.reason: Munna drifts beneath a crescent moon while two tiny Pidove sleep along the ledge below, easy to miss in Teeziro’s dreamy pink scene.
Munna keeps watch from a pastel canopy bed while Pikachu and Eevee snooze beneath the floral quilt. The sweetest little bedroom cameos.
Lapras drifts through a sunny lagoon, with Psyduck and its companions bringing a sleepy little cameo to the scene.
Snorlax is out cold under a comic-strip cloud of Zs, with Eevee tucked into the vintage snooze scene too.
Ursaring has become a giant forest mattress for its sleeping cub, Teddiursa. Protective parent, perfect pillow.
Joltik is wide awake on Yamper’s head, while the big dog has nodded off below. The real sleepy cameo is the one you might miss at first glance.
Leavanny looks after a whole leafy nursery, and two of the Sewaddle have already nodded off in their hoods. The third, and a grumpy Swadloon, are holding out.
Pachirisu is snoozing on Zeraora’s forehead while the electric powerhouse stays right in the middle of all that thunder.
Pikachu is having a perfectly nice day, but Psyduck has found a quiet spot by the water and is fully asleep. The little background nap is easy to miss on a first look.
Chansey is busy at the Pokemon Center while Snorlax has nodded off on the tiled floor. The whole room carries on around this absolutely unbothered snoozer.
Wigglytuff is wide awake in the sunny meadow, but the two Jigglypuff beside it are out cold. The supporting cast has made this a group nap, with Wigglytuff on pillow duty.
Jolteon keeps watch beneath the stars while Togepi sleeps against its chest and Rattata curls up nearby. A gentle guardian cameo for this shelf.
The Blueberry League Elite Four are in the middle of something, and Drayton has quietly checked out. He’s easy to miss up in the top-right corner of the table, asleep on his arm.
The twins and their flower crowns fill the whole card, so the sleeper hides at the edge: Mareep, half out of frame, snoozing under a flower of its own.
Your eye goes straight to Bebe at the keyboard. Glameow, stretched out beside the laptop with its eyes shut, is the cat nap hiding in plain sight.
Lillie and Clefairy are both awake. The sleeper is the small starry cloud between them: Cosmog has drifted off on the couch, sleep bubbles and all.

Most of the Skwovet lined up along the log are still chewing and grinning. One near the middle has stopped: eyelids drooping and cheeks still full, it’s nodding off mid-snack while Greedent keeps eating.
Reuniclus is having a splashy time in the shallows. Look up past it: a Duosion floats on its back across the top of the card, eyes closed, napping on the water.
Count the Swinub: one asleep on top of Light Piloswine’s head and three more dozing against its shaggy sides. Piloswine has become a hill for a family nap.
Two Natu have nested in Bouffalant’s afro. The one on the left is already asleep; its friend is keeping one eye open.
A finger is choosing who gets switched in, Hoppip is sweating it out, and Sentret has simply lain down in the middle circle and fallen asleep.

title: Snorlax, the Original Sleeper
description: Snorlax has been napping on Pokémon cards since 1998, and it has never once set an alarm. Here is every sleeping Snorlax in the collection, oldest to newest, plus one cameo where it nods off on the Pokémon Center floor.
seoTitle: Sleeping Snorlax Cards: Every Snorlax Nap, 1998–2026
metaDescription: All 21 sleeping Snorlax cards in the collection, from the 1998 Vending Machine contest card and Wizards Promo 49 to Fates Collide, 151 and Perfect Order, plus a Chansey cameo.

cards.reason: Where it all begins: a fan’s drawing that won CoroCoro’s 1998 contest, with Snorlax asleep in the middle of the road, exactly where its Pokédex says it might be.
The classic: out cold under the moon with comic-strip Z’s floating overhead. If you picture a sleeping Snorlax, you’re probably picturing this one.
Face-down among empty bottles and wrappers. Team Rocket’s Snorlax ate everything in reach and called it a night.
Up to its chin in a steaming hot spring, snowy mountains behind it. It is not getting out.
Face-down in a bed of white flowers, smiling. Possibly the gentlest nap in the collection.
The original printing of the Generations sleeper: Mitsuhiro Arita’s Snorlax, flat out in the grass two years earlier.
Just Snorlax, tall grass and nothing else. It dropped where it stood.
The only Snorlax nap that causes a stampede: it rolls through town fast asleep, and its attack hits harder while it’s Asleep.
Asleep under the trees with a Torchic on its head and two Pikachu nearby. Nobody is in a hurry to wake it.
Arms flung wide, mid-snore, in the dappled shade of a big tree. The afternoon nap, perfected.
A soft night sky and a cozy patch of ground. Classic bedtime.
Asleep on its side in the sunny grass, a paw tucked up by its face, in Atsuko Nishida’s warm storybook style.
Flat on its back under an apple tree, half-eaten apples all around. Food coma, case closed.
Blocking a real-world entrance, just like in the game. Please walk around.
Chin on its arm in a field of yellow flowers. Pure pastoral bliss.
Knitted in yarn by Asako Ito and caught mid-yawn on a felt-flower hill. A handmade nap.
Asleep by a pond while a Pidgey perches on its belly and a Diglett pops up nearby. Its own tiny ecosystem.
From the set that revisited the original 151: Snorlax dozing against a tree in the shade, exactly where you’d expect to find it.
Snoozing upright on the pavement outside a building, mouth wide open. Everyone else will just have to walk around.
Seen from its feet: Snorlax propped against a tree, head tipped back, out cold.
Knocked out among wild berries and mushrooms in Aya Kusube’s fairytale woods. Twenty-eight years in, still napping.
Bonus cameo: Chansey is hard at work in the Pokémon Center while Snorlax naps on the tiled floor.

title: Underrated Sleepy Pokemon Cards
description: Some of the sleepiest art in the Pokémon TCG hides in commons, stadiums and overlooked rares that sell for a few dollars or less. Here are twelve cards that deserve more love, including a Special Illustration Rare and two Illustration Rares that cost less than a booster pack.
seoTitle: Slept-On Sleeping Pokemon Cards: Underrated Budget Picks
metaDescription: Twelve slept-on sleeping Pokemon cards on a budget, including Poppy (Obsidian Flames SIR), Sina's Oranguru, Lycanroc and Togedemaru Illustration Rares, Koraidon, Slumbering Forest and Togetic.

cards.reason: Special Illustration Rares aren’t supposed to cost this little. Poppy, the smallest of Paldea’s Elite Four, has fallen asleep against her enormous Copperajah, and the size difference is the whole joke.
Siesta goals. Sina sleeps in a hammock while Oranguru lounges on a pile of pillows with a fan, berries and cold drinks within reach. Easy to miss in a Trainer Gallery full of bigger names.
Everyone looks at the fierce Lycanroc standing guard. The sleeper is the Rockruff curled up in the bottom corner, and somehow nobody is chasing this Illustration Rare.
One dozes by the tree, the other peeks over the grass to see what it’s missing. Orca’s sunlit glade deserves more fans.
Who looks at a Cosmoem card twice? You should: Lillie and Cosmoem are fast asleep side by side, a Pokémon that weighs more than a ton and the girl who carried it around in a bag.
If this site had a home address, it would be this glowing mushroom grove. Stadium cards rarely make it into art binders. This one should open yours.
Fire-type. Firewood. Fast asleep on top of it. Tomokazu Komiya made a common that deserves a frame.
Most people flip straight past uncommons. Flip back for this one: sui’s Togetic, asleep between pink blossoms in soft forest light.
Scarlet’s legendary, snoozing on a cliff edge above a waterfall like it has nowhere to be. Promos rarely get a second look, and this one has earned several.
Face-down on the pillow, Poké Ball abandoned on the bed. Tepig did not plan this nap. Easy to lose in a 236-card set, and one of the most relatable cards here.
Baby tucked into mom’s pouch, both of them dozing. One of Mitsuhiro Arita’s gentlest HeartGold & SoulSilver-era cards.
Find the one who’s asleep. In a cave full of flustered, squabbling Gible, one at the top has quietly slipped off for a nap.
